methods: Design: cross-sectional analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), 2011-2012. Population: Age >=18 years (analytic n = 2,783). Outcome: Eosinophilia - absolute eosinophil count >=0.5 x10^9/L. Exposure: mutually exclusive groups (Healthy controls, Toxoplasma gondii only, Toxocara only, Both positive), reference 'Healthy controls'. Analysis: prevalence ratios (survey-weighted Poisson regression), adjusted for Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Body mass index, Born in the United States. Variance: Taylor linearisation with strata and PSUs; weight WTSSTT2Y; design df = 17. Sensitivity analyses (5): Alternative outcome definition: AEC >=1.5; Logistic regression (odds ratio); Multiple imputation of missing covariates (m = 10); Alternative control group: everyone negative for all groups, no health screening (healthy-control bias check); Unweighted analysis (design ignored). Missing data: complete-case primary analysis; multiple imputation as sensitivity. Reporting: STROBE; plan pre-registered by hash before data access.

limitations.text: Cross-sectional: exposure and outcome are measured at the same visit, so the direction of association cannot be established.
Residual and unmeasured confounding cannot be excluded in an observational analysis.
Laboratory values come from a single blood or urine sample; transient abnormalities may be misclassified as persistent.

Healthy controls were screened for other diseases while exposure arms were not, which can exaggerate contrasts (healthy-control bias); an all-seronegative control group was run as a sensitivity analysis.
Sample size: underpowered for the target effect (from the run's design-based standard errors) (target PR 1.5); a null result is not evidence of no association.
3 comparisons against the reference group; nominal P values are not multiplicity-adjusted unless stated.
Raw values within plausible ranges: Out-of-range values: LBXSCR (1 low, 0 high); URDACT (0 low, 3 high)
NCHS presentation standards for proportions: 20 of 34 estimates meet the standard; 3 should be suppressed, 11 flagged for review.
Analyses use a laboratory subsample with its own weights; sample size and precision are lower than for the full MEC sample.

certainty.meaning: The true association may be substantially different from the estimate.

domains.reason: Cross-sectional design already reflected in the Low starting level; adjusted, pre-specified analysis with design audit passed.
Direction and inference stable across 2 sensitivity analyses.
US civilian non-institutionalised population; outcome measured directly.
95% CI 1.16-3.47 is wide (underpowered for the target effect).
Cannot be judged from a single study; pre-registration by plan hash reduces selective reporting.

certainty.caveat: GRADE rates bodies of evidence; this single-study rating summarises how much this analysis can contribute and should be re-rated in any systematic review.

assumptions: Outcome prevalence assumed 10% (run the blinded probe for the real rate band).
Design effect 1.8 (typical for NHANES; the post-run check uses the actual design-based SE).
Alpha 0.05 split across 3 comparisons with the control group (Bonferroni: 0.0167).
Group sizes unknown before the probe - showing the total sample needed for equal groups.
